TE2-F-01.hint: Choose one side, usually the more complicated one, and work only on that side until it matches the other. If you are stuck, rewrite everything in sines and cosines. Do not move terms across the equals sign.
slips: Starting from the whole equation and doing the same thing to both sides. Verifying means changing one side into the other.
Canceling a term that is added instead of multiplied, such as canceling \(\cos x\) in \(\dfrac{\cos x + 1}{\cos x}\).
Using a wrong Pythagorean identity, such as \(1 - \sin^{2}x = \sin x\).

TE2-A-01.hint: Combine fractions over a common denominator, or multiply the top and bottom by a conjugate such as \(1 + \sin x\). Then use \(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x = 1\) to simplify.
slips: Adding fractions by adding the numerators and the denominators.
Expanding \((1 + \cos x)^{2}\) as \(1 + \cos^{2}x\). The middle term \(2\cos x\) is lost.
Multiplying only the denominator by a conjugate.

parts.q: Verify that \(\csc u\tan u = \sec u\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\csc u\tan u\). Reciprocal and quotient identities: \(\dfrac{1}{\sin u}\cdot\dfrac{\sin u}{\cos u}\). Cancel \(\sin u\): \(\dfrac{1}{\cos u}\). Reciprocal identity: \(\sec u\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \((1-\sin \theta)(1+\sin \theta) = \cos^{2} \theta\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \((1-\sin \theta)(1+\sin \theta)\). Difference of squares: \(1-\sin^{2} \theta\). Pythagorean identity: \(\cos^{2} \theta\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \((\csc t-\cot t)(\csc t+\cot t) = 1\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \((\csc t-\cot t)(\csc t+\cot t)\). Difference of squares: \(\csc^{2} t-\cot^{2} t\). Pythagorean identity \(1+\cot^{2} t=\csc^{2} t\): \(1\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\sec \theta-\cos \theta = \sin \theta\tan \theta\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\sec \theta-\cos \theta\). Reciprocal identity: \(\dfrac{1}{\cos \theta}-\cos \theta\). Common denominator: \(\dfrac{1-\cos^{2} \theta}{\cos \theta}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} \theta}{\cos \theta}\). Factor: \(\sin \theta\cdot\dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\). Quotient identity: \(\sin \theta\tan \theta\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\tan t\cos t = \sin t\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\tan t\cos t\). Quotient identity: \(\dfrac{\sin t}{\cos t}\cdot\cos t\). Cancel \(\cos t\): \(\sin t\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{\sec t}{\csc t} = \tan t\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\dfrac{\sec t}{\csc t}\). Reciprocal identities: \(\dfrac{1/\cos t}{1/\sin t}\). Dividing by a fraction: \(\dfrac{1}{\cos t}\cdot\sin t\). Rewrite: \(\dfrac{\sin t}{\cos t}\). Quotient identity: \(\tan t\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\sin^{2} x-\cos^{2} x = 1-2\cos^{2} x\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\sin^{2} x-\cos^{2} x\). Pythagorean identity: \(\left(1-\cos^{2} x\right)-\cos^{2} x\). Combine like terms: \(1-2\cos^{2} x\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\csc t\tan t = \sec t\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\csc t\tan t\). Reciprocal and quotient identities: \(\dfrac{1}{\sin t}\cdot\dfrac{\sin t}{\cos t}\). Cancel \(\sin t\): \(\dfrac{1}{\cos t}\). Reciprocal identity: \(\sec t\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{\tan \theta}{\sec \theta} = \sin \theta\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\dfrac{\tan \theta}{\sec \theta}\). Quotient and reciprocal identities: \(\dfrac{\sin \theta/\cos \theta}{1/\cos \theta}\). Dividing by a fraction: \(\dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\cdot\cos \theta\). Cancel: \(\sin \theta\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\sin^{2} \theta-\cos^{2} \theta = 1-2\cos^{2} \theta\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\sin^{2} \theta-\cos^{2} \theta\). Pythagorean identity: \(\left(1-\cos^{2} \theta\right)-\cos^{2} \theta\). Combine like terms: \(1-2\cos^{2} \theta\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\sin^{2} u-\cos^{2} u = 1-2\cos^{2} u\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\sin^{2} u-\cos^{2} u\). Pythagorean identity: \(\left(1-\cos^{2} u\right)-\cos^{2} u\). Combine like terms: \(1-2\cos^{2} u\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \((1-\sin x)(1+\sin x) = \cos^{2} x\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \((1-\sin x)(1+\sin x)\). Difference of squares: \(1-\sin^{2} x\). Pythagorean identity: \(\cos^{2} x\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{\sin u}{1+\cos u}+\dfrac{1+\cos u}{\sin u} = 2\csc u\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\dfrac{\sin u}{1+\cos u}+\dfrac{1+\cos u}{\sin u}\). Common denominator: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} u+(1+\cos u)^{2}}{(1+\cos u)\sin u}\). Expand: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} u+1+2\cos u+\cos^{2} u}{(1+\cos u)\sin u}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{2+2\cos u}{(1+\cos u)\sin u}\). Factor: \(\dfrac{2(1+\cos u)}{(1+\cos u)\sin u}\). Cancel: \(\dfrac{2}{\sin u}\). Reciprocal identity: \(2\csc u\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{1-\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = \dfrac{\sin \theta}{1+\cos \theta}\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the right side, \(\dfrac{\sin \theta}{1+\cos \theta}\). Multiply top and bottom by \(1-\cos \theta\): \(\dfrac{\sin \theta(1-\cos \theta)}{(1+\cos \theta)(1-\cos \theta)}\). Difference of squares: \(\dfrac{\sin \theta(1-\cos \theta)}{1-\cos^{2} \theta}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{\sin \theta(1-\cos \theta)}{\sin^{2} \theta}\). Cancel: \(\dfrac{1-\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\). This is the left side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{\sin \theta}{1+\cos \theta}+\dfrac{1+\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = 2\csc \theta\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\dfrac{\sin \theta}{1+\cos \theta}+\dfrac{1+\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\). Common denominator: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} \theta+(1+\cos \theta)^{2}}{(1+\cos \theta)\sin \theta}\). Expand: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} \theta+1+2\cos \theta+\cos^{2} \theta}{(1+\cos \theta)\sin \theta}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{2+2\cos \theta}{(1+\cos \theta)\sin \theta}\). Factor: \(\dfrac{2(1+\cos \theta)}{(1+\cos \theta)\sin \theta}\). Cancel: \(\dfrac{2}{\sin \theta}\). Reciprocal identity: \(2\csc \theta\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}+\dfrac{1+\cos x}{\sin x} = 2\csc x\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}+\dfrac{1+\cos x}{\sin x}\). Common denominator: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} x+(1+\cos x)^{2}}{(1+\cos x)\sin x}\). Expand: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} x+1+2\cos x+\cos^{2} x}{(1+\cos x)\sin x}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{2+2\cos x}{(1+\cos x)\sin x}\). Factor: \(\dfrac{2(1+\cos x)}{(1+\cos x)\sin x}\). Cancel: \(\dfrac{2}{\sin x}\). Reciprocal identity: \(2\csc x\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\sin \theta\cos \theta(\tan \theta+\cot \theta) = 1\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\sin \theta\cos \theta(\tan \theta+\cot \theta)\). Quotient identities: \(\sin \theta\cos \theta\left(\dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}+\dfrac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\right)\). Distribute and cancel: \(\sin^{2} \theta+\cos^{2} \theta\). Pythagorean identity: \(1\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{\cos x}{1-\sin x} = \dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\dfrac{\cos x}{1-\sin x}\). Multiply top and bottom by \(1+\sin x\): \(\dfrac{\cos x(1+\sin x)}{(1-\sin x)(1+\sin x)}\). Difference of squares: \(\dfrac{\cos x(1+\sin x)}{1-\sin^{2} x}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{\cos x(1+\sin x)}{\cos^{2} x}\). Cancel: \(\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\tan u+\cot u = \sec u\csc u\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\tan u+\cot u\). Quotient identities: \(\dfrac{\sin u}{\cos u}+\dfrac{\cos u}{\sin u}\). Common denominator: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} u+\cos^{2} u}{\cos u\sin u}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{1}{\cos u\sin u}\). Split: \(\dfrac{1}{\cos u}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sin u}\). Reciprocal identities: \(\sec u\csc u\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\sin u\cos u(\tan u+\cot u) = 1\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\sin u\cos u(\tan u+\cot u)\). Quotient identities: \(\sin u\cos u\left(\dfrac{\sin u}{\cos u}+\dfrac{\cos u}{\sin u}\right)\). Distribute and cancel: \(\sin^{2} u+\cos^{2} u\). Pythagorean identity: \(1\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{1-\cos u}{\sin u} = \dfrac{\sin u}{1+\cos u}\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the right side, \(\dfrac{\sin u}{1+\cos u}\). Multiply top and bottom by \(1-\cos u\): \(\dfrac{\sin u(1-\cos u)}{(1+\cos u)(1-\cos u)}\). Difference of squares: \(\dfrac{\sin u(1-\cos u)}{1-\cos^{2} u}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{\sin u(1-\cos u)}{\sin^{2} u}\). Cancel: \(\dfrac{1-\cos u}{\sin u}\). This is the left side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{\cos u}{1-\sin u} = \dfrac{1+\sin u}{\cos u}\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\dfrac{\cos u}{1-\sin u}\). Multiply top and bottom by \(1+\sin u\): \(\dfrac{\cos u(1+\sin u)}{(1-\sin u)(1+\sin u)}\). Difference of squares: \(\dfrac{\cos u(1+\sin u)}{1-\sin^{2} u}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{\cos u(1+\sin u)}{\cos^{2} u}\). Cancel: \(\dfrac{1+\sin u}{\cos u}\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\tan \theta+\cot \theta = \sec \theta\csc \theta\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\tan \theta+\cot \theta\). Quotient identities: \(\dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}+\dfrac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\). Common denominator: \(\dfrac{\sin^{2} \theta+\cos^{2} \theta}{\cos \theta\sin \theta}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{1}{\cos \theta\sin \theta}\). Split: \(\dfrac{1}{\cos \theta}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sin \theta}\). Reciprocal identities: \(\sec \theta\csc \theta\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.

parts.q: Verify that \(\dfrac{1}{1-\sin t}+\dfrac{1}{1+\sin t} = 2\sec^{2} t\) is an identity.
parts.a: Start with the left side, \(\dfrac{1}{1-\sin t}+\dfrac{1}{1+\sin t}\). Common denominator: \(\dfrac{(1+\sin t)+(1-\sin t)}{(1-\sin t)(1+\sin t)}\). Simplify: \(\dfrac{2}{1-\sin^{2} t}\). Pythagorean identity: \(\dfrac{2}{\cos^{2} t}\). Reciprocal identity: \(2\sec^{2} t\). This is the right side, so the identity is verified.
